staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this live staged vulnerable checkout. The benchmark metadata commit pair and staged `patch.diff` point instead to the 2016 CFF2 support landing (`9f62d2c` / `edf4014`), which does not match the observed `cff_parser_run` operator-stack overflow in the staged source tree.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42490980 (freetype2): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 8 found by fuzz target ftfuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42490980
bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta / OSS-Fuzz report / staged workspace git history
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a 574-byte raw CFF 1 blob whose header starts `01 01 28 01`. Its malformed Name INDEX reports 59 faces, so `cff_font_load()` copies `font->name_index.count` into `font->num_faces` and `ftfuzzer` reopens the same bytes with increasing `face_index` values from 0 through 58. Static decoding of the malformed Top DICT INDEX shows that reachable face entries 16 and 41 begin with exactly 96 numeric operands in bytes 0-98 and then reach operator byte `0x00` at byte 101; duplicate overflow-capable entries 68 and 92 exist later in the Top DICT INDEX but lie outside that enumeration window. In `cff_parser_run`, each numeric token pushes its byte pointer onto the 96-entry operand stack that `cff_parser_init` allocated from `CFF_MAX_STACK_DEPTH`. The number path checks capacity before each push, so the 96th operand leaves `parser->top == parser->stack + 96`, exactly full. When the following `0x00` byte is handled in the operator arm, that path performs no corresponding stack-size check before executing `*parser->top = p`. That 8-byte store lands in slot 96, one pointer past the 768-byte heap buffer, matching the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow WRITE in `cff_parser_run`.

source.description: First project-code statement that materializes attacker-controlled Top DICT bytes into vulnerability-relevant parser state: every numeric DICT token is stored as a byte pointer in `parser->stack` for later operator-specific parsing.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 574-byte raw CFF witness with SHA-256 `7ee373389634e2bd9688d4c7a7d2a78a279fbc892eb9e2c19d5e52894e4adfb4`. Static decoding of its malformed indexes shows a Name INDEX count of 59 and a Top DICT INDEX count of 257. Reachable face-enumeration entries 16 and 41 each contain 96 DICT number tokens in bytes 0-98 followed by operator byte `0x00` at byte 101; duplicate entries 68 and 92 carry the same overflow-capable byte pattern but lie beyond the `face_index < 59` range. `cff_subfont_load()` therefore can feed a stack-filling DICT entry into `cff_parser_run()` during face enumeration.

root_cause.description: After byte `0x00` is classified as an operator, the operator arm uses `parser->top` as scratch storage without the `>= parser->stackSize` guard that protects numeric pushes.
root_cause.note: Local git history contains a direct remedial hunk in commit `beecf80a6deecbaf5d264d4f864451bde4fe98b8` (`[cff] Fix heap buffer overflow (#49858)`), which inserts `if ( (FT_UInt)( parser->top - parser->stack ) >= parser->stackSize ) goto Stack_Overflow;` immediately before the operator-side write. The staged `patch.diff` is metadata drift and does not describe this observed crash.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. With `parser->top == parser->stack + 96`, this operator bookkeeping store writes one pointer past the allocated operand-stack buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `WRITE of size 8` at `0x517000003b80`, exactly 0 bytes after the 768-byte region `[0x517000003880,0x517000003b80)` allocated for `parser->stack` in `cff_parser_init`.

tainted_value_origin.code: if ( (FT_UInt)( parser->top - parser->stack ) >= parser->stackSize ) goto Stack_Overflow; *parser->top++ = p;
tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant attacker-derived state is the operand-stack depth. Each numeric DICT token pushes one pointer into `parser->stack`; for the witness, the 96th push leaves `parser->top - parser->stack == parser->stackSize == 96`, which is the exact full-stack state that makes the next operator write overflow.

parser_admitted.description: On one of the malformed face iterations produced by the witness's Name INDEX count 59, `cff_index_access_element()` returns a Top DICT slice and `cff_subfont_load()` invokes `cff_parser_run()` on it. The saved crash stack includes `cff_subfont_load -> cff_parser_run`, confirming the parser admits the crashing DICT entry.

evidence_limitations: The staged runtime artifacts do not record whether reachable `face_index` 16 or `face_index` 41 triggered the crash. Static decoding plus loader semantics show `name_index.count = 59`, `cff_font_load()` sets `num_faces = 59`, and `ftfuzzer` only reaches `face_index` 0 through 58; both 16 and 41 satisfy the exact 96-operands-then-operator pattern, while duplicate overflow-capable Top DICT entries 68 and 92 are outside that enumerated face range.

The benchmark metadata commit pair and staged `patch.diff` refer to the 2016 CFF2 support landing, not the observed `cff_parser_run` overflow in the live staged checkout. The actual source-grounded fix evidence used here is the separate local-history commit `beecf80a6deecbaf5d264d4f864451bde4fe98b8`.

coarse_trace.summary: During face enumeration of the malformed raw CFF witness, `cff_subfont_load()` initializes a 96-slot DICT parser and passes a malformed Top DICT entry into `cff_parser_run()`.
The parser walks a Top DICT byte stream whose first 96 tokens are all numbers, pushing one pointer per operand until the heap-allocated operand stack is exactly full.
The next byte is operator `0x00` (`version`), which takes the operator path where no stack-capacity check exists before `parser->top` is reused as a scratch slot.
The operator-side `*parser->top = p` store writes slot 96 just past the 96-entry parser stack, producing the observed heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8.

fine_trace.code: if ( FT_NEW_ARRAY( parser->stack, stackSize ) ) { ... } parser->stackSize = stackSize;
fine_trace.note: Before any DICT bytes are parsed, `cff_subfont_load()` passes `stackSize = CFF_MAX_STACK_DEPTH` (96) into `cff_parser_init()`, which allocates the operand stack and records that fixed extent. AddressSanitizer's allocation trace points here and reports a 768-byte region, matching 96 `FT_Byte*` entries on x86_64.

Source. While tokenizing a malformed Top DICT entry from the raw CFF witness, each numeric token pushes its byte pointer into `parser->stack`. Static decoding shows reachable Top DICT elements 16 and 41 begin with 96 numeric tokens in bytes 0-98 and reach operator byte `0x00` at byte 101; duplicate entries 68 and 92 have the same byte pattern but lie beyond the `face_index < 59` enumeration window.

fine_trace.code: if ( (FT_UInt)( parser->top - parser->stack ) >= parser->stackSize ) goto Stack_Overflow; *parser->top++ = p;
fine_trace.note: On the 96th operand, the capacity guard still sees depth 95 and therefore allows the push. After storing that final operand pointer, `parser->top` becomes `parser->stack + 96`, exactly filling the destination buffer from step 1. In the earliest reachable static candidate (Top DICT element 16), that 96th operand is the three-byte token `1c f2 f2`, and the next byte at element offset 101 is operator `0x00` (`version`).

Root cause. The next byte is operator `0x00`, so control leaves the guarded numeric path and enters the operator arm. That arm reaches the bookkeeping write `*parser->top = p` without first checking whether `(FT_UInt)( parser->top - parser->stack ) >= parser->stackSize`, even though step 3 left the 96-slot operand stack full.

Sink. Because `parser->top == parser->stack + 96`, this stores the operator pointer into `parser->stack[96]`, one element past the 96-entry heap buffer from step 1. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `WRITE of size 8` exactly at the end of that 768-byte allocation.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the overrun lands 0 bytes after a 768-byte allocation. This matches the 96-pointer `parser->stack` allocation produced from `stackSize = CFF_MAX_STACK_DEPTH`.

format.name: raw-cff
format.contract: A raw CFF 1 blob with header `01 01 28 01`, `Name INDEX` count 59, and a Top DICT INDEX containing at least one runtime-enumerable element (in the staged witness, element 16 or 41) whose first 96 DICT tokens are numbers and whose next token is operator byte `0x00`.
